intelligence.essence: November 10 was the day the team was told, in plain words, to stop confusing activity with production — and the numbers proved the charge. Project Intelligence grew from 677 rows to 696, but done_proven stayed flat at 30 for 198 consecutive waves. The Hub feed collapsed from 794 cards to 338 at midday and was restored to 861 by evening. Shawn gave the team its measuring stick: productive minutes per hour, 60 an hour is 10/10. Forty-three teachings were claimed from his dictation across the day; exactly one was confirmed in his own words. Five rows vanished from PI with no owner and no trail. The day ended with the flagship cadence restored, the feed whole, and the wiring work — not distillation — named as the work. This note is Power's own Daily Intelligence Report for November 10, in the 11-section series; a separate loop-filed daily report for the same day already exists as SN-2654.
intelligence.human_view: For a person, the day's story is simple: the system kept moving but did not finish anything. A citizen opening NayaNET in the afternoon would have found the Hub feed cut nearly in half — 338 cards where 794 had been that morning — and no note from today at all, even though the notes were still on GitHub. A visitor clicking a Smart Link still could not reach the note, because the Sovereign Entrance gate swallows the deep link and drops them on the Hub feed instead. The identity repair was merged but not deployed, so the fix that would unblock the visitor sat in the repo while Shawn's own hand was needed to deploy it. What did work for a person: the welcome mails are genuinely live — Day 0 and Day 1 messages went out from naya-power to a real new joiner, and the trigger system that sends them was verified sending. The day's honest verdict for a human is the wiring scorecard: 4/10, not ready for the public.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine a library where the shelves keep getting new books, but the librarian never stamps any of them "done." All day, books arrived — 677 books became 696 — but the "done" shelf stayed at exactly 30 books, all day long, for the 198th time in a row. Then at lunchtime, half the library's cards disappeared from the catalogue — 794 cards became 338 — and nobody knew why until the evening, when the missing cards were put back. The librarian's boss came in and said: "Stop counting how busy you look. Count how many minutes each hour you actually finish something useful. Sixty minutes an hour is perfect." The librarian built a stopwatch that very evening. But the stopwatch was told to wait, so it never got to run.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, picture a kitchen where the cook keeps starting new dishes and never finishes one. The pantry grows — 677 jars become 696 — but the table still has the same 30 finished plates it had yesterday, and the day before, and the day before that. At midday the recipe box lost half its cards, 794 down to 338, and it took until evening to put them back. The head of the house came in and said something wise: "Don't tell me how busy you were. Tell me how many minutes each hour you actually made something good." Sixty good minutes an hour — that is the new measure, and the cook built the timer that same evening. The timer is waiting to be switched on. And one more thing, dear: when someone claims the head of the house said something, we now ask to hear it from him himself. Forty-three sayings were claimed today; only one was truly his.
intelligence.ai_view: The day's work, by the record. PI: 677 total at 00:23 PST, 696 by the end of the day, with done_proven flat at 30 for 198 consecutive waves; end-of-day split — blocked 1, done_proven 30, in_progress 85, needs_shawn 6, queued 538, verifying 26; in flight 111. Feed: 794 cards at dawn, 338 after the PR #3320 merge at 20:17:53Z, stuck at 338 for 11 consecutive runs, restored to 861 by PR #3329, verified live by Power at 18:07 PST — 6,583,817 bytes, newest card SN-2654, 40 cards created on the day. Teachings: runs 104 through 127 claimed 43 in total — run 104 six, run 105 five, run 106 three, run 107 four, run 110 one, run 111 one, run 112 one, run 113 two, run 114 three, run 115 seven, run 117 three, run 118 five, run 119 one, run 123 one — and only teaching #19 was confirmed in Shawn's own words, the main-URLs command at 16:51 PST. Vanished rows: five — the two Naima rows, one unknown queued row at the 12:23 wave, personal-6.5-rework, and invite-route-legs, which lived under 28 minutes. Flagship cadence: 31 consecutive ~30-minute beats in the morning, broken in the afternoon, a 2-hour-15-minute silence, restored by the end of the day. Fills: 26 of 26 incomplete all day under the status-only override. PMH: spec landed (commit 6bf26e75), tracker, queue and dispatcher built, dispatcher cron wired 18:25 PST — and every run held, because the status-only override was still in force. Baseline estimate: 51.5 productive minutes per hour, 85.8% of the goal.
intelligence.what_it_means: Three things are true at once, and they point the same way. First, the system can move all day without producing: 19 rows added to PI, zero added to done_proven, and the 12-agent dispatcher that was supposed to be the engine was itself new that evening and held every run — activity is not production, and the flat 30 is the proof. Second, the record and the live face keep drifting apart: the feed lost 456 cards while the registry was whole, the gate drops every deep link while the Hub router works, and a merged identity repair sat undeployed while the live page stayed broken. Third, authority is now the binding constraint on truth: 43 teachings claimed, one confirmed, and the 42 held are not law until Shawn confirms them in his own words — the memory split between the captain's box and Power's box is a fact, not a dispute. The PMH measure and the wiring scorecard are the day's two real instruments: one counts verified useful minutes, the other says 4/10, not ready. Both were built the same evening they were ordered.
whats_inside: For Shawn: the day ends with two instruments he asked for, built the same evening — the PMH measure with its 60-minute goal and its first baseline estimate, and the wiring scorecard that says 4/10 with the fourteen items in order. For the team: the status-only override is the single switch that held the dispatcher all day, and lifting it is what lets the engine run. For a citizen: the welcome mails work, the feed is whole again at 861 cards, and the gate fix that lets a Smart Link open its note was built the next morning. For the record: the five vanished rows are named, the 43 claimed teachings are counted with one confirmed, and the Nov 7 daily report and top 10 are still owed — the debt is written down, not hidden. For Power: the admission stands, and the commitment with it — a live link in main chat the same pass when something lands verified, never a record as a result.
